sara: Heads-up — after the int8 bring-up for llama-3-small-v2 our BERTScore on english-pairs/dev dropped ~0.06 vs fp16. Embedding L2 norms shifted ~12% on average.

mohan: I saw a small change in pass@k for code tasks? Or is that unchanged?

sara: pass@k for code is fine, it's mostly BERTScore and the calibration curves for multi-choice that look off. Could be metric sensitivity to embedding magnitude.

alex: Quick question — are we normalizing embeddings before computing BERTScore in the eval runner? Our bertscore wrapper historically assumed normalized vectors. :thinking: 

sara: Runner is currently feeding raw model embeddings into the bertscore binary. Previously we normalized in the pipeline, but the quant model returns different norms and we didn't update the runner.

eva: Can you paste the failing asserts and the command you used to run the eval?

sara: Sure — here's the smoke command and the failing lines from pytest.
```
# smoke run
python -m eval.runner --suite english-pairs --model llama-3-small-v2:int8 --metrics bertscore,exactmatch

# failing snippet (condensed)
E       AssertionError: assert 0.63 >= 0.69
E        +  where 0.63 = compute_bertscore(raw_pred_emb, raw_ref_emb)
E        +  where 0.69 = reference bertscore (fp16 baseline)
```

matt: CI note: failures only show up on the dedicated-quant job, fp16 CI passes. So it's not test flakiness, it's a model/metric mismatch in the quant path.

ci-bot: @matt retriggered job: https://ci.example.com/jobs/4572 (started) :robot_face: 

mohan: Proposal: L2-normalize embeddings inside the bertscore impl and make normalization idempotent. Also add a regression test that compares cosine similarity between fp16 and quantized embeddings and gates on a small delta.

alex: SGTM. Patch idea: normalize right before cosine computation and document a model manifest flag `embeddings_normalized` to avoid double-normalizing. Example patch: 
```python
# eval/metrics/bertscore_wrapper.py
def compute_bertscore(pred_emb, ref_emb):
    # ensure embeddings are unit norm so bertscore is invariant to magnitude shift
    pred = pred_emb / (np.linalg.norm(pred_emb, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12)
    ref = ref_emb / (np.linalg.norm(ref_emb, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12)
    return cosine_similarity(pred, ref)
```

sara: Also need to avoid double-normalize if model already outputs unit vectors. Suggest adding `embeddings_normalized: bool` in model manifest and checking it in the runner: if true, skip normalization.

matt: For CI gating, add a smoke assertion: 
```yaml
# ci/smoke-quant.yml snippet
checks:
  - name: embedding-norm-regression
    script: python -m eval.tools.check_norms --model quant --baseline fp16 --threshold 0.03
```
The script should compute mean_norm across a sample and fail if |mean_norm_quant - mean_norm_fp16| > 0.03.

eva: Dashboard request: add per-model 'embedding mean norm' chart and a comparison metric 'BERTScore (normalized) vs BERTScore (raw)'. Make it visible on model onboarding page.

mohan: I'll open a PR that: 1) updates bertscore impl to idempotently normalize, 2) adds the `embeddings_normalized` manifest flag and runner wiring, 3) adds a unit test that compares cosine sims between quant vs fp16 (threshold 0.02), 4) CI smoke check yaml, and 5) small docs note about calibration impact.

sara: Also add a calibration check for exact-match distributions — we saw slight shift in confidence histograms for multi-choice. Maybe add a brier score check on the eval harness.

mohan: Good call. I'll include a brier score smoke test in the same PR.

alex: @mohan please tag me on the PR, I'll review the impl and the perf/alloc implications (normalization is cheap but we should vectorize).

matt: Once PR lands, I'll add the dashboard panels and update the onboarding checklist to include embedding-norm smoke.

eva: Thanks all. Nice catch. :thumbsup:

sara: Assigning to @mohan. Thanks for the quick triage everyone.

mohan: Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval/pull/842 (draft) — will update with test outputs.

ci-bot: build 4572 completed (quant smoke) — results posted in PR comments.

alex: Looking at the draft, we might also add a tiny numerical stability change (eps to 1e-9) to avoid underflow on tiny vectors.

mohan: Noted, will update.

sara: Follow-up: after applying normalization patch locally, bertscore matches baseline within 0.01 on the dev set. Planning to run full eval overnight.

eva: Great. We'll monitor dashboard.

matt: Closing the loop later today. :white_check_mark:
